sections.title: Training Progression Parameter Adjustments
sections.content: Discussed adjustments to training progression parameters — quality workouts increased to 12 while long runs remained at 10-12 miles, prompting review and potential adjustment of long run range to 14-16 miles. Ben explained gap filling logic in the sandbox: one infill at the beginning for onboarding time, another at the end to align taper timing with race day.

sections.title: Two-Week Taper Training Approach
sections.content: Aligned on a two-week taper structure where the last day is race day. Final week includes a moderate quality workout and an easy long run. While timing of certain workouts may shift, the consistent two-week approach remains effective and is standard for most athletes — may extend to three weeks for athletes with health issues.

sections.title: Running Schedule Structure Optimization
sections.content: 4 consecutive days of running is less ideal than alternating with rest days. Agreed to implement a warning system for non-ideal scheduling patterns and present pre-defined ideal weekly formats (top 3-4 preferred schedules for 3-7 days) rather than fully custom configurations.

sections.title: Pain Feedback Guidelines
sections.content: When runners report pain, the app should advise seeking medical help rather than preventing plan generation. Agreed to differentiate between manageable pain and serious issues. Revised wording to ask whether pain is something the runner can run through or if it's affecting their ability to run effectively.

sections.title: Cross-Training and Recovery Guidelines
sections.content: When users reach the lowest tier due to consecutive days off, cross-training should be recommended indefinitely. For MVP, keeping cross-training guidance simple without specifying activities. A 10K requires two recovery days before a stressor; a half marathon needs at least four recovery days.

sections.title: Athlete Mileage Management Rules
sections.content: Discussed managing athletes reporting fatigue three consecutive times within two weeks — results in a tier reduction and reduced mileage, with the option to keep them at current levels. Emphasized building thoughtful rules for prompting athletes about readiness, noting this approach also helps train AI models.

sections.title: Weight and Running Performance Analysis
sections.content: Discussed how modern running shoes allow heavier runners to perform well. Observed that heavier runners often have higher power numbers than faster runners — losing weight while maintaining power could significantly improve performance.

sections.title: Workout App Development Timeline
sections.content: Agreed to focus on half marathon feature first before adding marathon. Targeting January 1st for MVP release instead of August, allowing more time for testing and business planning. Complexity lies more in testing and infrastructure than coding.

sections.title: Runner Training Plan Assignment Process
sections.content: Explored how to determine appropriate tiers for runners whose current and desired days per week differ. Suggested using clear rules like miles per week to decide the appropriate tier. Agreed to use a 3-month average for determining typical running days and mileage.

sections.title: New Runner Onboarding Strategy
sections.content: Agreed to start with conservative estimates and use a feedback mechanism to adjust. Focusing on the median runner rather than edge cases. Building a flexible system that gathers data to improve future iterations. Most runners would likely start at or near their current level.

sections.title: Training Mileage Tracking System
sections.content: Discussed a spreadsheet system with separate low and high columns for each day to show mileage possibilities. Agreed on using separate columns rather than hybrid values for simplicity. Formulas calculate weekly mileage ranges and long run percentages.

sections.title: Runner Training Transition Strategy
sections.content: Creating a gradual transition path for runners increasing from 4 to 5 to 6 days per week without losing built-up training. Agreed on an intervention after three consecutive weeks of maximum mileage to ask runners if they want to add a day or increase mileage.

sections.title: Onboarding Plan Frequency Improvements
sections.content: Modified options to include ranges like '3-4 days', '4-5 days', '5-6 days', and '6-7 days' to give participants more flexibility. Additional days kept optional throughout the plan, particularly for the 4-5 day range.

sections.title: Onboarding Questionnaire Simplification
sections.content: Using three main categories — 'Feel Great', 'Feel Tired', 'In Pain' — instead of numeric scales. Provides clearer guidance and triggers appropriate actions. Postponing specific body part information for MVP.

sections.title: High-Risk Injury Status Determination
sections.content: Number of separate injuries costing a week or more of training in the last year determines tier reduction. Each qualifying injury results in a one-tier drop. Age-based adjustments excluded from MVP due to complexity.

sections.title: Training Plan Algorithm Development
sections.content: Explored structuring mileage progression considering weekly mileage, running days, and long run distances. Working backwards from desired levels more effective than formula-based prediction. Plan allows pacing increases rather than sudden jumps.

sections.title: AI Running Training App Development
sections.content: Using long run distance as the primary determinant for quality runs and weekly mileage ranges. Easy runs calculated based on established parameters. One-mile-per-day increase approach up to five days per week. Intervention mechanisms needed for pain reports and plan adjustments.

sections.title: Electrolyte Drink Development
